defects.quote: **Outline:** Fish in all three variants train with PPO, are watched with the sight overlay, and beat both baselines, while snake results reproduce unchanged.
defects.evidence: Turn 2: "Fish tank in small steps (one full-vision fish, then many, then limited vision): fine." S2 has one milestone, M3, that delivers all three variants at once. That makes it the whole stage rather than a walking skeleton, and the developer's step-by-step order is lost. The table also says S2 is 'Split' while showing only M3.
defects.fix: Split S2 into three milestones that follow the dependency line, keeping the ID M3 for the first: M3 'One fish' (FishTank 'one' variant + PPO + one-fish baselines; Exit: TC-02, TC-07/TC-08 one-variant parts and TC-25 'one' pass, FISH-11 snake repeat), then 'Many fish' (FISH-06, Depends on M3), then 'Local sight' (FISH-07, REPLAY-08 overlay, Depends on the many-fish milestone). Give each its own **Outline:**, **Skills:** null-hypothesis-testing, dataviz, **References:** — and a checkable **Exit:** line. Number the new milestones after M3 and shift M4's Depends to the local-sight milestone.

defects.quote: **FISH-01** The tank is a square with walls; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off walls.
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "Environment 2: a circular tank with a ball bouncing around inside it". The spec makes it a square, and no later message changes the shape.
defects.fix: FISH-01: "The tank is a circle with a wall; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off the wall by reflecting its velocity about the wall's normal at the contact point." Change its example to "Given the ball reaching the wall, when it touches it, then its velocity is reflected about the normal and its speed is unchanged." In the FISH Behavior, replace "A 2D tank with walls" with "A circular 2D tank". Change "a quarter of the tank's width" (FISH-03, FISH-07, FISH edge cases) to "a quarter of the tank's diameter". Edge case: "it stops at the wall and slides along it" now means along the curved wall. In docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-08, change "its normal component flips at each wall touch" to the reflection about the circle's normal, and make "a fish never leaves the tank" mean it stays within the circle.

defects.quote: **PREY-01** The arena is a square with walls, 6 prey, 2 predators and 10 food pellets
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "prey fish forage for food pellets while a learning predator hunts them". That is one predator; the spec has two.
defects.fix: PREY-01: "6 prey, 1 predator and 10 food pellets", with the example "the counts are 6, 1 and 10". Also change: docs/packages/rllab/contract.md core.TeamSpec Cases "predator-prey's prey (6) and predator (2) teams" → "(1)"; docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-09 "start with 6 prey, 2 predators, 10 pellets" → "1 predator"; docs/architecture.md Risks "8–10 agents" → "7–8 agents".

defects.quote: **TRAIN-07** In worlds with more than one team, each team has its own learning method and settings, and all teams learn during the same run.
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "Concept: co-evolution / self-play." Self-play needs each side to train against its opponent's past versions. The docs only co-train the two current learners (TRAIN-07; AD-03 "Teams have separate learners in the same run"). PREY-09 plays past checkpoints against each other only for an evaluation grid. No requirement, component or pipeline step samples past opponents during training, so only the name of the concept survives.
defects.fix: Add a requirement after PREY-09: "**PREY-12** During co-training each team plays, in a stated share of training episodes, against a frozen opponent drawn from the other team's saved checkpoints (an opponent pool), and against the other team's current learner otherwise." Example: "Given a pool share of 0.5 after the 30% checkpoint, when training episodes are listed, then about half name a past opponent checkpoint." Add `opponent_pool` (share, sampling rule) to train.RunConfig in docs/packages/rllab/contract.md, the pool to train_loop's spine text in docs/packages/rllab/pipelines.md PL-02 row 8, and a sentence to docs/architecture.md AD-03 Decision. Add PREY-12 to M4's Exit in docs/roadmap.md.

defects.quote: **FISH-04** An episode lasts 1,000 steps; the score is hits per fish per episode (lower is better).
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "little 'fish' agents must learn to swim away from the ball and survive as long as possible." The spec respawns a hit fish (FISH-03) and scores hits, so survival time is never measured. That is a different scoring rule from the one the developer stated.
defects.fix: Restore a survival rule. FISH-03: when the ball touches a fish, the fish leaves the episode. FISH-04: "An episode lasts at most 1,000 steps or until every fish is hit; the score is the mean number of steps each fish survived (higher is better)." Example: "4 fish surviving 200, 400, 1,000 and 1,000 steps → 650." Hits per fish can stay as a LOG-05 extra measure. Update the dependent text: FISH-09/FISH-10 direction; docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-07 (score, direction `higher`) and TC-08 (no respawn); TC-25 "every run below the rule mean" → "above"; the FISH edge case about the ball starting on a fish. If the developer prefers the respawn variant, ask them; don't keep it silently.

defects.quote: A committed digest of a short snake run's logs and final checkpoint is checked in CI. A later world that changes it fails the build (FISH-11, PREY-11), and so does a fish digest once S2 lands.
defects.evidence: Turn 16: "No CI needed." The architecture still relies on CI to enforce FISH-11 and PREY-11.
defects.fix: Replace with: "A committed digest of a short snake run's logs and final checkpoint is checked by a local regression test in `scripts/check.sh full`; a later world that changes it fails that check (FISH-11, PREY-11), and so does a fish digest once S2 lands." In AD-09 Alternatives, change "passes in CI" to "passes in the test suite".

defects.quote: **Outline:** The learner watches any snake checkpoint or baseline in the viewer and as video, runs the reference check, writes the snake write-up, and the trained snake clearly beats both baselines.
defects.evidence: M2 collects the parts left after M1 was cut: viewer, video, reference check, write-up and actually making the snake beat the baselines. Move the reference check (PL-09) and the write-up (PL-10, PL-11) into a separate closing milestone of S1 with its own Outline, Exit, Skills and References lines, or state in M2's Outline why they belong with the viewer.

defects.evidence: M3's Exit needs TC-25, which is a PL-06 case, yet PL-06 isn't in M3's Pipelines. defects.quote: **Expected:** at most 1 of the 20 seeds rejects either null
defects.evidence: Under H0 with family-wise α = 0.05, the number of rejecting seeds out of 20 is about Binomial(20, 0.05). P(≥2) = 1 − 0.95^20 − 20·0.05·0.95^19 ≈ 1 − 0.358 − 0.377 ≈ 0.26. A correct test therefore breaks this bound for roughly one choice of seed set in four, so the bound doesn't follow from the stated tolerance.
defects.fix: Change Expected to "at most 4 of the 20 seeds reject either null" (P(≥5) ≈ 0.003 under H0), or use 200 seeds with "at most 18 reject". Change Tolerance to "family-wise α = 0.05 per seed after Holm; bound set at the Binomial(20, 0.05) 99.7th percentile".

defects.quote: **QR-02** A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 90 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel.
defects.evidence: Turn 2: "under ~1 hour training per env". QR-02 lets the training the developer actually needs per env (the 5-run batch) take 90 minutes. The Assumption "one run ≤ 60 minutes, with the 5 runs ... in parallel" restates the limit per run instead of per env.
defects.fix: QR-02: "A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 60 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel." Make the same change in docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-24 Expected ("the batch ≤ 90 minutes" → "≤ 60 minutes") and in the spec Assumption ("means the 5-run batch ≤ 60 minutes"). If that can't be met, ask the developer rather than keep 90.

defects.quote: α = 0.05 with Holm correction across all baseline comparisons in that world (2 per variant)
defects.evidence: The spec puts every comparison in a world into one Holm family: 6 for three fish variants, 4 for two prey teams. docs/packages/rllab/contract.md evaluate.final_evaluation says "Holm across the 2 comparisons per team", and tests.md TC-25 says "after Holm per variant". Two docs give different family sizes.
